The gonadosomatic index (GSI) of female Chocolate hind (Cephalopholis boenak) was measured from gonad samples. Field studies in the South China Sea at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C] recorded a mean gonadosomatic index of 3% [GSI = 3%]. This relatively modest value suggests that females invest a small proportion of somatic tissue into gamete production at any single sampling point, consistent with the intermittent spawning strategy observed in many small groupers. The total length of an individual at the end of its growth period was estimated from extensive mark-recapture records as 30 centimeters [Li = 30 centimeters], placing this species among the smaller members of the genus Cephalopholis. These data were collected across multiple reef sites characterized by coral cover typical of inshore habitats, where food availability and predation pressure shape the asymptotic size of resident fishes.

The onset of sexual maturity in Cephalopholis boenak is marked by a distinct transition in both length and mass. Histological examination of gonadal tissue indicated that the total length at which fifty percent of individuals achieve puberty is 12.2 centimeters [Lp = 12.2 centimeters], a size attained after roughly one to two years of benthic life. Correlating with this length, the corresponding wet weight at puberty was recorded as 25.8 grams [Wwp = 25.8 grams], derived from length-weight regressions based on over two hundred specimens. Interestingly, the body mass at this reproductive milestone is orders of magnitude greater than the wet weight at birth, which was estimated from the diameter of pelagic eggs. Based on a mean egg diameter of 0.95 millimeters, the calculated wet weight at birth is 0.000449 grams [Wwb = 0.000449 grams], reflecting the tiny, yolk-dependent larvae that emerge during the pelagic phase. This extreme disparity between neonatal and pubertal mass underscores the substantial somatic growth required before reproductive competence is achieved.

Larval development begins with the release of pelagic eggs, and the time elapsed from fertilization to the emergence of the yolk-sac larva depends heavily on ambient temperature. In Cephalopholis boenak, under controlled laboratory conditions where water temperature was maintained at a stable 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C], the age at birth was determined to be 5.5 days [ab = 5.5 days]. This short incubation period is typical of tropical serranids and facilitates rapid progression through the vulnerable early life stages. Following hatching, the lecithotrophic larva relies on endogenous yolk reserves before transitioning to exogenous feeding, a critical bottleneck that governs larval survival in the plankton. The species exhibits a maximum adult wet weight of 398 grams [Wwi = 398 grams], a figure derived from the length-weight relationship that accounts for the full somatic growth potential of the species, representing the ultimate body mass achieved by long-lived individuals in productive reef environments.

Population longevity estimates for Chocolate hind were derived from otolith increment analysis of individuals collected across several Philippine reef sites. Under the prevailing water temperature regime of 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C], the maximum recorded lifespan was determined to be 4745 days [am = 4745 days], which is equivalent to approximately thirteen years. This relatively extended lifespan for a grouper of its size suggests a life-history strategy characterized by steady adult survival and iteroparous reproduction across multiple seasons. In mature females the gonadosomatic index was 3% [GSI = 3%] at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C]. The wet weight at puberty of 25.8 grams [Wwp = 25.8 grams] represents only a small fraction of the ultimate wet weight of 398 grams [Wwi = 398 grams], indicating a prolonged period of post-pubertal somatic growth that likely enhances fecundity at larger sizes.

The total length at puberty, measured at 12.2 centimeters [Lp = 12.2 centimeters], marks the size at which females first become capable of spawning, though the transition from the pelagic larval stage begins much earlier. The total length of 30 centimeters [Li = 30 centimeters] serves as the upper asymptotic value for this species, beyond which further increase in body length is negligible despite continued mass gain. The maximum longevity of 4745 days [am = 4745 days] at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C] underscores the species capacity to persist in stable reef habitats, where annual mortality is balanced by consistent recruitment from the pelagic larval pool. Females are capable of producing multiple clutches across spawning seasons, and the wet weight at birth of 0.000449 grams [Wwb = 0.000449 grams] represents the starting point of an ontogenetic trajectory that culminates in a 398 gram [Wwi = 398 gram] adult, highlighting the substantial energetic investment required to bridge the gap between a pelagic larva and a territorial benthic predator.
